He established himself at Tours, where he ministered to a small and often hidden flock through years of pagan hostility, gathering his people in secret to celebrate the sacred mysteries.
He labored there some fifty years and died about the year 301, the first bishop of a see later made illustrious by St. Martin. He was buried in the Christian cemetery of the city.
saints.knownFor: The apostle and first bishop of Tours.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. Anastasius I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: A pope praised by Jerome for his holiness, who condemned the errors drawn from the writings of Origen…
biography: Anastasius I was elected pope in 399 and, though his reign was short, he was esteemed for his poverty of life and his pastoral zeal. He condemned the errors that certain readers were drawing from the works of Origen, a controversy that divided his friends Jerome and Rufinus.

St. Jerome, who knew him, praised his holiness and said that Rome did not deserve to keep so good a bishop long, for he was soon taken away. He died in 401 and was buried in the cemetery of Pontian on the Via Portuensis.
saints.knownFor: Condemning Origenism and his repute for holiness among the Fathers.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. Dominic of Silos
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A Spanish abbot who rebuilt the monastery of Silos and was long invoked by mothers and by captives…
biography: Dominic was born in Navarre about the year 1000 and served as a shepherd before becoming a Benedictine monk and, later, prior. Exiled after a dispute with the king over the monastery's lands, he was received in Castile and made abbot of the decayed monastery of Silos, which under him rose to new splendor of learning, art, and observance.

He was renowned for ransoming Christians held captive by the Moors and for miracles of healing, and he died at Silos in 1073. Long afterward it was at his shrine that Bl. Joan of Aza prayed before the birth of her son, whom she named Dominic — the founder of the Order of Preachers.
saints.knownFor: Restorer of the abbey of Silos and helper of captives and mothers.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 December

saints.name: St. Peter Canisius
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The Jesuit catechist called the Second Apostle of Germany, whose catechisms held countless souls to the faith…
biography: Born at Nijmegen in 1521, Peter Canisius became the first Dutchman to enter the Society of Jesus and gave his life to the renewal of the Catholic faith in the German lands during the upheavals of the Reformation. He preached, founded colleges, took part in the Council of Trent, and served as a tireless envoy of popes and bishops.

Above all he wrote catechisms, adapted for children, students, and adults, which were translated many times and taught the faith to whole generations. He died at Fribourg in Switzerland in 1597, and was canonized and declared a Doctor of the Church in 1925.
saints.knownFor: His catechisms and the defense of the faith in Germany.

canonization.canonized: 1925 by Pope Pius XI, who declared him a Doctor of the Church

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Peter Canisius (vatican.va)

saints.name: St. Chaeremon and the Martyrs of Egypt
saints.title: Bishop and Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: An aged Egyptian bishop and the many Christians who perished in the deserts fleeing the persecution of Decius…
biography: During the persecution of the Emperor Decius about the year 250, great numbers of Christians in Egypt fled into the deserts and mountains rather than deny their faith, and there many died — some of hunger, cold, and hardship, some by wild beasts, and some at the hands of robbers and raiders — so that all were counted martyrs.

Among them was Chaeremon, the very aged bishop of Nilopolis, who fled with a companion into the mountains and was never seen again. Their story is preserved in a letter of St. Dionysius of Alexandria, quoted by the historian Eusebius.
saints.knownFor: The confessors and martyrs of the Decian persecution in Egypt.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. John of Kanty
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Polish priest and professor of Kraków, famed for learning matched by humility and boundless charity to the poor…
biography: John was born at Kęty in Poland in 1390 and became a priest and a distinguished professor of theology at the University of Kraków. For a time he served as a parish priest, then returned to the university, revered by students and colleagues alike for the soundness of his teaching.

He was known even more for his austerity of life and his charity, giving food and clothing to the poor and living in great simplicity. He died at Kraków in 1473 and was canonized in 1767; he is honored as a patron of Poland and of teachers.
saints.knownFor: A learned and charitable priest, patron of Poland and of scholars.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 October

saints.name: St. Delphinus
saints.title: Bishop of Bordeaux
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop of Bordeaux who baptized St. Paulinus of Nola and opposed the Priscillian heresy…
biography: Delphinus was bishop of Bordeaux in Gaul in the late fourth century. He took part in the councils that condemned the Priscillianist heresy, at Saragossa and again at Bordeaux, and he is best remembered as the bishop who baptized and guided St. Paulinus of Nola, who ever after wrote to him with the affection of a spiritual son.
A friend of St. Ambrose as well, he labored for the peace and orthodoxy of the Church in Aquitaine and died about the year 403.
saints.knownFor: Baptizing St. Paulinus of Nola and opposing Priscillianism.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. Anastasia
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An ancient martyr honored at the dawn Mass of Christmas, whose name is spoken in the Roman Canon…
biography: Anastasia was a martyr of the early fourth century, put to death, according to her ancient acts, in the persecution of Diocletian at Sirmium in the Roman province of Pannonia. Her relics were later brought to Constantinople and to Rome, where a church on the Palatine bears her name.

Because that church was long a station for the second Mass of Christmas, offered at dawn, St. Anastasia has for many centuries been commemorated on 25 December, and her name is remembered in the Roman Canon among the holy martyrs.
saints.knownFor: The martyr commemorated at the Christmas dawn Mass.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. Stephen
saints.title: The First Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The first of the seven deacons and the first martyr of the Church, who saw heaven open as he was stoned…
biography: Stephen, “full of faith and of the Holy Ghost,” was one of the seven chosen by the Apostles to serve the poor of the Jerusalem community. Bold in preaching, he was seized and, before the council, beheld the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand. He was cast out and stoned, praying for his killers — among whom stood the young Saul.
He is the first martyr (protomartyr), honored the day after Christmas.
saints.knownFor: The Church's first martyr; deacon of Jerusalem.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 26 December

saints.name: St. John
saints.title: Apostle and Evangelist
saints.shortBlurb: The beloved disciple who leaned on the Lord's breast, stood by the Cross, and wrote the fourth Gospel…
biography: John, son of Zebedee and brother of James, was among the first called and one of the three closest to the Lord. He is “the disciple whom Jesus loved,” who leaned upon His breast at the Supper, stood by the Cross to receive His mother, and was first to believe at the empty tomb.
Tradition ascribes to him the fourth Gospel, three Epistles, and the Apocalypse, and holds that he lived to great age at Ephesus — the only Apostle not to die a martyr.
saints.knownFor: The beloved disciple; author of the fourth Gospel.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 December

saints.name: The Holy Innocents
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The children of Bethlehem slain by Herod in his rage against the newborn King, the first to die for Christ…
biography: When the wise men did not return to tell him where the child was, King Herod, fearing a rival to his throne, ordered the killing of all the boys of Bethlehem and its neighborhood who were two years old and under, as the Gospel of Matthew relates. The Holy Family had already fled into Egypt at the warning of an angel.

The Church honors these little ones as martyrs — flowers of the martyrs, in an ancient phrase — who died for Christ though they could not yet speak His name. Their feast falls within the octave of Christmas.
saints.knownFor: The infant martyrs of Bethlehem, first to die for Christ.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. Thomas Becket
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The chancellor turned archbishop of Canterbury, who defended the Church's liberty against his king and was murdered at his own altar…
biography: Thomas Becket, born in London in 1118, rose to be chancellor and close friend of King Henry II of England, and in 1162 was made archbishop of Canterbury. To the king's surprise he then took up the cause of the Church's freedom against royal encroachment, and the quarrel drove him into six years of exile in France.

Soon after his return, on 29 December 1170, four of the king's knights cut him down in Canterbury Cathedral. The whole of Christendom was shaken; he was canonized within three years, and his shrine at Canterbury became one of the great pilgrimages of the Middle Ages.
saints.knownFor: Martyred archbishop who defended the liberty of the Church.

canonization.canonized: Canonized in 1173 by Pope Alexander III

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 29 December

saints.name: Pope St. Felix I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: A pope of the third century who governed the Roman Church in a time of peace between persecutions…
biography: Felix I was elected bishop of Rome in 269 and governed the Church during the reign of the Emperor Aurelian. His pontificate fell in a period of comparative peace, and he is associated in ancient records with the care of the tombs of the martyrs and with a statement of the faith concerning the person of Christ, sent to the East during the controversy over Paul of Samosata.
He died in 274 and was buried, according to the old Roman calendars, in the cemetery of Callixtus on the Appian Way.
saints.knownFor: A third-century pope of the Roman Church under Aurelian.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)

saints.name: St. Sylvester I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The pope of the peace of the Church under Constantine, in whose reign Nicaea met and the great Roman basilicas rose…
biography: Sylvester I was pope from 314 to 335, during the reign of the Emperor Constantine, when the Church emerged at last from three centuries of persecution into freedom and favor. In his time the first great basilicas of Rome — the Lateran and Old St. Peter's — were built, and the first ecumenical council met at Nicaea in 325 to define the faith against Arius, the pope sending legates in his place.

Little is known with certainty of Sylvester himself, and much later legend gathered about his name, but his long pontificate spans the turning of the Roman world toward Christ. He died in 335 and, kept on the last day of the year, is remembered across much of Europe on the night that bears his name.
saints.knownFor: Pope during the age of Constantine and the Council of Nicaea.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 31 December
